doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Piano, organ and rock bands before harmonica
summary: He started piano at eight, studied classical piano at Manhattan School of Music, played pipe organ and rock, and took up harmonica at 18.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you start playing gigs as a pianist before the harmonica became, you know, your instrument that you became known for I guess?

Well I started out on piano when I was eight. I studied classical piano at the Manhattan School of Music for four years on Saturdays, for four years. And so I was playing piano. And then I studied the pipe organ. I went to a private school that had a pipe organ. I did that for two years. I played a whole bunch of Bach with the foot pedals and the whole bit. But then I started playing rock & roll and I was in my high school rock band you know. I played the Farfisa organ and piano and I only started playing harmonica when I was 18.
